name: Study load with generation
desc: Study large loads and hybrid facilities together with generation, to site them efficiently and cut network upgrades.

letters.desc: AEMA supports modeling interconnection studies on a facility's actual controlled operating profile rather than worst-case peak withdrawal, consistent with broader stakeholder calls to reflect real withdrawal rights and curtailment commitments.
quotes: interconnection studies must reflect the actual, controlled operating profile of a facility rather than a theoretical maximum withdrawal.

letters.desc: ACORE agrees with studying load and hybrid facilities alongside generating facilities to improve efficiency and lower network upgrade costs, and wants common forecasting methods built into planning.
quotes: the Commission to work with DOE and the National Laboratories to establish best practices and common methodologies for the forecasting of large loads and their power needs that can be incorporated into the long-term transmission planning process.
ACORE agrees with the ANOPR recommendations to study load and hybrid facilities together with generating facilities as a means to improve the process efficiency and lower network upgrade costs

letters.desc: Bloom backs the ANOPR proposal to study large load and co-located generation together, citing Brattle analysis showing potential to avoid billions in transmission costs.
quotes: Like the ANOPR, Brattle finds that an integrated interconnection study approach for new load and new generation based on requested firm withdrawals and injections can significantly reduce the need for transmission upgrades, potentially avoiding billions in transmission expansion costs.

under existing rules, load is studied as if it seeks firm rights to withdraw 100% from the transmission system to meet its requirements, while the generator is studied as if it seeks to inject 100% of its capacity into the transmission grid, with some RTOs, like PJM, requiring that generator capacity also be studied for deliverability to load throughout the system.  These bifurcated, non-integrated processes ignore on-site supply benefits and can improperly identify required Network Upgrades, resulting in slower interconnection and unnecessarily increasing Network Upgrade costs.

letters.desc: Load and hybrid facilities should be studied together with generation, accounting for their operating characteristics and enabling efficient siting that minimizes network upgrades.
quotes: The Commission should ensure that the study process reflects the expected operating characteristics of the generation (or energy storage) and the load. The study process should provide a pathway for load and hybrid facilities to request that flexibility and specific operating characteristics be incorporated into study assumptions. Solutions that incorporate load flexibility (including hybrid configurations of load including generation or energy storage) should be treated on equal footing as traditional transmission infrastructure solutions.

letters.desc: CEBA supports jointly studying load and supply-side interconnection customers. Coordinated studies can identify more cost-effective transmission solutions and reduce the multiple-submission behavior that inflates queue volumes and delays both load and generator projects.
quotes: CEBA strongly supports the ANOPR proposal to jointly study supply-side and large-load interconnection customers where practicable.

letters.desc: ClearPath endorses joint processing of large load and generation interconnection requests to align commercial timelines for offtake agreements and to enable identification of shared transmission solutions. This approach ensures that all customers benefiting from a transmission upgrade contribute to its cost.
quotes: ClearPath strongly supports the ANOPR's proposal to jointly study supply-side interconnection customers and large load interconnection customers to the extent practicable.

Coordinating interconnection studies for large loads with supply-side interconnection can enable the identification of more cost-effective transmission solutions and ensure that all benefiting customers pay, whether they are load or supply customers.

letters.desc: Constellation asks FERC to adopt clear, uniform large load forecasting standards so planning baselines reflect only credible, committed projects. The filing proposes requiring verifiable commitments before including loads in planning models.
quotes: the Commission should adopt clear, uniform standards, which should also consider large load forecasting standards and other measures that will expedite large load studies and interconnections.

letters.desc: Constellation supports studying load and generation together under ANOPR Principle 3. The LCEP proposal operationalizes joint study by building on already-completed studies at existing POIs, reducing the need for new network upgrade analyses.
quotes: All such study processes must be tailored to accommodate speed to service or the efficiencies of siting at Points of Interconnection already proven to be reliable will be lost.

The Commission should also require Transmission Providers to clearly identify the studies for evaluating LCEP Service requests. Clear and transparent rules on the studies performed by Transmission Providers are critical to prevent delay.

LCEP Service also is fully responsive to the ANOPR's directives and principles, including to study load together with Generating Facilities, given "siting a large load near or at the same point of interconnection as a new generating facility could reduce the network upgrades needed to interconnect only the load or only the generating facility" (Third Principle), and incentivizing co-location which can "ensure[] efficient buildout of the transmission system" (Fifth Principle).

letters.desc: The filer recommends that hosting-capacity-style data publication and standardized joint-study paths cover both load and hybrid or adjacent supply at the same point of interconnection, reducing soft costs and directing requests to viable locations.
quotes: Systematize and automate flexible interconnections by requiring publication of hosting‑capacity‑style data for load (hourly and seasonal headroom, constraints, expected curtailment windows) and by offering standardized flexible options (limited‑load profiles, non‑firm service, and joint‑study paths for hybrid or adjacent resources)

Create a non‑firm network service (withdrawal) option and allow non‑firm injection for hybrid or adjacent resources participating in LLFCs, with joint study for load and supply at or near a common point of interconnection

letters.desc: Crusoe supports studying load and generation together for hybrid facilities. Joint studies produce a more accurate picture of net grid impact and reduce the need for costly network upgrades.
quotes: Joint interconnection studies for hybrid facilities that bring new generation with load will expedite the interconnection process and minimize the need for costly and time-consuming construction of network upgrades because the impact of the new load can be offset by the addition of new generation.

Hybrid facility structures cause significantly less impact on the transmission grid than large loads that do not bring generation.  Thus, where hybrid facilities are proposed, the load and generation should be studied together to get an accurate picture of the load's impact on the grid.

letters.desc: DCC supports studying new load and new generation together to capture system benefits, reduce duplicative studies, and align net impact with interconnection costs.
quotes: DCC advocated for studying new load and new generation together to capture system benefits.

letters.desc: DEC asks FERC to require a single integrated study process for co-located generation and load, eliminating duplicative separate studies that increase costs and slow development.
quotes: The Commission should require transmission providers to establish a single, integrated interconnection process under their OATTs for projects that combine generation and load at the same point of interconnection.

Current procedures force developers to complete separate studies for generation and load, even when they are part of a single co-located facility. This duplication increases costs, creates conflicting assumptions, and slows project development.

letters.desc: DPN supports the joint-study approach in the ANOPR, pointing to AI firms re-energizing idled generation and siting data centers nearby so loads are not studied in isolation.
quotes: load and hybrid facilities should be studied together with generating facilities. Such an approach will allow for efficient siting of loads and generating facilities and thereby minimize the need for costly network upgrades.

letters.desc: EDF supports studying co-located load and generation together because joint studies can reduce the need for costly network upgrades and shorten time to energization. EDF also flags that current study processes do not accurately model storage resources and asks that this gap be fixed.
quotes: A bifurcated or tiered review process should be implemented, allowing low-impact loads that are inherently less likely to cause significant transmission system upgrades to be studied and brought online more quickly than higher-impact loads.

interconnection studies should better utilize storage assets in interconnection requests.  Currently, interconnection studies do not accurately model real time operating characteristics of storage resources, which limits opportunities for storage resources to be deployed to serve large load needs.

It is appropriate for large loads and hybrid facilities to pay for network upgrades required for their interconnection and transmission service based on their rights-based interconnection obligations.  As noted above, hybrid facilities should be able to benefit from reduced network upgrade costs by studying co-located generation and load together.

letters.desc: ELCON supports coordinating the large load interconnection queue with the generator interconnection process to improve load forecasting and siting decisions.
quotes: Coordinating the generator interconnection process with the large load interconnection process would, in itself, improve load forecasting as well as siting decisions, as recognized in the ANOPR.

letters.desc: ECA strongly agrees that large loads and any generation they are developing should be studied together. Linking the two in interconnection and planning processes is one of the top benefits the Commission can deliver.
quotes: Aligning load interconnection and generator interconnection and better incorporating large load growth into transmission planning are the two biggest benefits action on the ANOPR can provide.
ECA strongly agrees with the need for study processes to more closely link new large loads with the new generation resources that they may wish to construct or contract.

letters.desc: Enchanted Rock supports a joint study process that studies co-located load and generation together based on net impacts, arguing it more accurately models flexible system capabilities and optimizes existing infrastructure.
quotes: Enchanted Rock encourages the Commission to adopt rules that will facilitate joint study processes (even if only for a provisional period) and that evaluate co-located and hybrid facilities based on their net impacts to the grid.

a joint study process would allow LCDG and hybrid facilities to be studied based on their operational behavior and net load impacts, which Enchanted Rock believes will result in less strain on the transmission system, unlock available grid headroom, optimize existing transmission infrastructure and more accurately model the flexible capabilities of the system.

letters.org: Enerwise Global Technologies, LLC dba CPower
letters.desc: Principle 3 should expand to allow joint study of large loads with load flexibility and other incremental resources. This enables faster assessment by combining resources that deploy at different timelines.
quotes: The Joint Parties suggest revising principles three, five, and seven as discussed below. Principle three states that 'to the extent practicable, load and hybrid facilities should be studied together with generating facilities'. This principle should be expanded to allow for study with other types of incremental resources, including load flexibility, in the appropriate location.

letters.desc: ENGIE strongly supports studying large loads, hybrid facilities, and generating facilities together for a more complete picture of grid impacts. It cites SPP's Coordinated Planning Process as a model worth emulating.
quotes: ENGIE strongly supports this principle. We believe that a more holistic approach to system planning, including the studying of all types of facilities together, provides a more complete picture of how new facilities will interact with the electric grid.
ENGIE would like to highlight the Southwest Power Pool's ("SPP") soon to be implemented Coordinated Planning Process ("CPP") for being the most robust, holistic planning process of any ISO/RTO.

letters.desc: Eolian has directly experienced refusals by grid operators to study load and proximate generation together, resulting in duplicative and avoidable upgrade requirements. It supports a coordinated study process that considers hybrid facility load and generation jointly to minimize network upgrade costs and study timelines.
quotes: Eolian has experienced multiple cases where a transmission provider's refusal to perform an integrated study of load and generation has caused duplicative upgrade requirements that could have been avoided if load and generation had been considered together, which has impacted the business viability of both load and generation.

serial streamlined study of load and hybrid facilities is possible where the facility nominates operating limits (in MW) for aggregate net injections and withdrawals of power, installs necessary control equipment to ensure that the facility is capable of following the dispatch controls of the transmission system operator and balancing authority and respecting operating limits at all times, and is capable at any time of complete self-supply or otherwise curtailing the load such that the facility can take transmission service on a non-firm basis.

letters.desc: Eolian defends the feasibility of integrated joint study of hybrid generation and load, rebutting concerns from Constellation and Entergy. It clarifies that joint study means studying both components together within the same model, including contingency events for each component separately, not merely studying the net of the two.
quotes: Consistent with ANOPR Principles Three, Five, and Six, integrated joint study of hybrid load and generation facilities based on requested withdrawal and injection rights is critical to enabling rapid, affordable interconnection of large loads and hybrids.
The load and generation components of a hybrid facility are no different and would be separately subject to such contingency studies under a joint study approach.

letters.desc: Eolian endorses a joint or coordinated study process and asks at minimum that generators be able to nominate associated loads for inclusion in their interconnection study, with consistent standards applied across all transmission providers.
quotes: the Commission can require load and generation study coordination even if it decides against asserting jurisdiction over load interconnection by requiring transmission providers to coordinate in generation interconnection study processes with the relevant transmission owners or electric distribution companies conducting load interconnection studies.
the Commission should require consistent standards for when and how load is included in generator interconnection studies.

letters.desc: esVolta endorses the ANOPR's proposal to study large loads and hybrid facilities together with identified generating facilities, and specifically extends that support to paired BESS configurations.
quotes: If an ANOPR is issued, it should seek to include a proposal that articulates core principles, such as studying large loads and hybrid facilities together with generation where practicable, recognizing curtailable and dispatchable configurations (including those supported by BESS) for expedited treatment, and aligning cost responsibility with the specific injection and withdrawal rights requested.

Studying large loads together with BESS aligns closely with the Department's emphasis on the timely and orderly interconnection of large loads. Where a large load is electrically proximate to BESS that is designed to provide the services described above, the combined configuration is better able to satisfy applicable reliability and power quality criteria without imposing excessive incremental burdens on the transmission system.

letters.desc: Google supports a coordinated, joint study process for electrically proximate load and generation that accounts for how both resources plan to operate together, consistent with Order No. 2023's treatment of storage resources.
quotes: The coordinated and expedited study of electrically proximate large loads and grid-connected generators will facilitate the development of digital infrastructure while minimizing the strain on, and maximizing the use of, existing power infrastructure.

letters.desc: Google agrees with the DOE ANOPR framing that load and generation interconnection requests that are related should be studied together, aligning project timelines and reducing piecemeal upgrade decisions.
quotes: the record is clear: to get large load interconnection right, the Commission must consider the interplay between transmission capacity and the interconnection of both large loads and the generators that supply them.

The way to address that foundational transmission issue is to adopt a holistic transmission planning process that optimizes grid development by accounting for both generators and the large loads planning to interconnect.

letters.desc: GridStor supports the ANOPR proposal to study paired load and generation together but asks that the load side, including ESR charging, be included so paired ESRs and large loads are studied as a single coordinated resource rather than competing for transmission capacity. It recommends ESR charging be studied during the generator interconnection process before the agreement is executed.
quotes: In particular, we ask that any Commission consideration of such coordinated study include the load side of paired facilities like ESRs, not only the generation side.

The present approach to studying loads independently creates a competitive dynamic between any paired ESR and large loads, forcing them to vie for transmission capacity rather than provide desired mutual benefit.
The Commission should enable studies of large loads and paired ESRs as coordinated loads, i.e., with integrated control that act as a single resource.

Therefore, we recommend that the Commission consider whether study of ESR charging should be more optimally conducted during the generator interconnection process and prior to a generator interconnection agreement, instead of in a separate load study after a generator interconnection agreement.

letters.desc: The filing goes further than the ANOPR by urging FERC to require large loads to pair with new generation as a condition of interconnection, not merely to study them together where practicable. Paired generation should be sited within the same market area to minimize transmission system costs.
quotes: The ANOPR should expressly include discussion of requiring large load to be matched with equivalent new generation in order to connect to the federal transmission system.

New load and generation may be sited at the same point of interconnection (i.e. hybrid facilities), but to minimize costs on the transmission system they should be sited within the smallest applicable market area even if they are not at the same point of interconnection.

letters.desc: Interconnection studies should go beyond independent customer behavior and include coordinated cyber-physical attack scenarios, developed with NERC, Department of Defense, E-ISAC, and RTO/ISO planners.
quotes: I recommend that large‑load interconnection procedures mandate probabilistic and scenario‑based studies that include coordinated cyber‑physical attack cases, not just independent customer behavior cases, and that these scenarios be developed in consultation with agencies like NERC, Department of Defense, E‑ISAC, and RTO/ISO planners.

letters.desc: iMasons urges FERC to work with NERC and transmission providers to establish clear, consistent national technical standards for large load interconnection to reduce project delays and reliability risks.
quotes: iMasons urges the Commission to work with NERC and transmission providers to expedite the development of clear and consistent technical standards that will govern the interconnection of large loads nationally.

letters.desc: IECA fully supports simultaneous interconnection studies covering both a Data Center and its associated generation resource as offsetting loads, viewing this as the core mechanism for expedited approvals and efficient grid buildout.
quotes: We submit that a collaborative approach between States and the Commission can produce a process that can simultaneously study both a Data Center and a contractually-associated electric generation resource by joining both (i) the Federal approval of interconnection of the generation resource (through the Commission-regulated LGIP and LGIA process) and (ii) the State approval (through a State-regulated utility) of the interconnection of a new large load.

We fully support the proposal in the ANOPR of simultaneously studying the impacts on the network of one or more large loads (i.e., Data Centers) and one or more associated electric generating facilities as offsetting loads and resources and therefore worthy of expedited consideration and approval as a reasonable approach to addressing the interconnection of Data Centers that co-locate with existing or new electric generation facilities.

letters.desc: IECA supports the ANOPR proposals to study co-located load and generation impacts simultaneously and to approve both interconnections expeditiously, subject to adequate grid protections.
quotes: We support the simultaneous study of system impacts from a Co-Located Load with its Co-Located Generation and the expeditious approval of the interconnection of both at a single point of interconnection or at two or more "proximate" points of interconnection, provided that the impacts on the transmission grid and other users of that transmission grid are addressed as set forth in Section III.B. of these Reply Comments.

letters.org: Invenergy Wind Development North America LLCInvenergy Solar Development North America LLCInvenergy Thermal Development Holdings LLC ,
letters.desc: Invenergy supports studying load, hybrid facilities, and generation in one interconnection queue rather than separate tracks. Separate study produces unnecessary network upgrade identifications, overlooks cheaper regional solutions, and deprives generation developers of useful load timing information. A common queue would match generation to load and reduce ratepayer costs.
quotes: Load and hybrid interconnection requests should be studied in the existing generator interconnection queue(s) with generator interconnection requests and not in a separate large load queue.
studying load and generation separately can, and often does, result in the identification of network upgrades that would not be needed had the facilities been studied together.

load interconnections, unlike generator interconnection requests, are studied exclusively by each transmission owner and typically only include transmission solutions in that particular transmission owner's footprint, the study process often overlooks potentially less-expensive transmission solutions that would have been identified by looking at the system more holistically

letters.desc: Longroad supports studying load and generation together and updating the study base case with all known confirmed load so that network upgrade needs are accurately sized from the start.
quotes: The base case should be updated for all known and confirmed load, which will minimize piecemeal build -- at least until Open Access 2.0 principles are adopted.

letters.desc: LS Power supports requiring joint interconnection studies for hybrid facilities that interconnect electrically close together. Coordinated study ensures upgrades are sized correctly, avoids redundant infrastructure, and supports resource adequacy analysis.
quotes: The Commission should require that hybrid facility (large load and associated matching generation) interconnections with the interstate transmission grid be studied together where they are anticipated to interconnect electrically close to each other.

letters.desc: The Maryland PSC supports studying large load together with new generation and storage, finding that simultaneous addition of matched supply maintains market prices and minimizes the need for network upgrades.
quotes: Bringing new (large) load on simultaneously with a matching amount of new generation/storage would maintain the supply/demand balance existing on the grid, thus causing minimal impact to the marginal cost of energy and capacity and lessening the need for network upgrades.

letters.desc: The filer supports allowing data centres to negotiate bespoke contracts with network companies under regulatory oversight, so that connection studies and cost-sharing arrangements reflect project-specific conditions rather than uniform rules.
quotes: Data centres could negotiate bespoke contracts with network owners and/or operators, under regulatory approval. These contracts could be used to get the data centres to contribute to the local network to the best of its ability and could result in lower costs for the energy company and lower risks for other grid users.

letters.desc: Meta agrees that large loads should be studied jointly with generating facilities, using composite behavior analysis, provided that joint study processes do not delay large load interconnection.
quotes: Meta also agrees with the ANOPR's recommendation in paragraph 20 that large load be studied together with generating facilities such as by studying 'the composite behavior of co-located load and generation' so long as joint study processes do not delay the interconnection of large loads

letters.desc: Microsoft backs studying large loads and generation together, arguing it speeds interconnection, improves grid planning, and can shrink the scale and cost of transmission upgrades. It frames the most useful reforms as those that boost speed-to-market and cut network-upgrade cost and scope.
quotes: Microsoft believes studying load and generation together has the potential to speed up the interconnection process for load and generation by eliminating duplicative, and potentially conflicting, studies and will facilitate more efficient grid planning by more closely aligning generation capacity needs with large loads.
Additionally, studying load and generation together potentially reduces the scale and cost of transmission upgrades by minimizing system impacts and the need for major backbone reinforcements.

In Microsoft’s view, the changes ripe for consideration are those that (i) focus on processes that will increase speed-to-market for new customers and new generation and (ii) reduce the cost and scope of network upgrades needed for interconnection.

letters.desc: The filing calls for a load queue that explicitly conditions interconnection on the ability to provide reliable service, which requires adequate generation capacity. The ANOPR's failure to include this requirement is identified as a central gap.
quotes: The ANOPR does not propose to include a requirement in the interconnection procedures for large loads, that interconnection of large loads to the grid must be predicated on the ability to provide reliable service which in turn requires generation capacity which in turn means that there should be a load queue. The NOPR should include such a requirement.

letters.org: Natural Resource Defense CouncilSustainable FERC ProjectClean Air Task Force ,Coalition for Affordable Utility Services and Energy Efficie ,EARTHJUSTICE ,ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENSE FUND ,MONTANA ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION CENTER ,Sierra Club ,Southern Environmental Law Center ,
letters.desc: The filers support studying large loads together with generation to minimize network upgrade needs, provided the process is transparent enough to enable accurate cost allocation and does not disadvantage existing queue participants.
quotes: FERC must ensure that load interconnection studies are sufficiently rigorous and transparent to identify the beneficiaries of network upgrades and enable cost-allocation that is roughly commensurate with the benefits.

letters.desc: OPSI sees merit in studying co-located load and generation together, noting it could create incentives for large loads to bring their own generation resources.
quotes: If large load additions come with its own generation and FERC promotes the more efficient study of generation and load together, this could be an incentive for these loads to bring their own generation.

letters.desc: SMA strongly endorses the ANOPR principle that loads and hybrid facilities be studied alongside generators, because the current siloed approach leaves real risks unaddressed on both sides.
quotes: SMA strongly supports the simulation of load and hybrid facilities together as we find large gaps today in addressing the risks on both the grid and AI data center (load) sides, in that the load-side ignores real risks to the grid and vice versa.

letters.desc: SEIA supports joint study of load and associated generation but wants the Commission to allow each region to integrate large-load studies into its existing queue rather than creating a separate queue. Studies must capture the actual operational profile of each load, including islanding capability and curtailability, to avoid underestimating needed upgrades.
quotes: SEIA recommends that the Commission allow flexibility in how these studies are conducted and prioritized so that they align appropriately with each region's existing queue and study procedures.
any study of the large load and associated generation, whether co-located or not, must reflect the actual operational needs of the load.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The group supports joint study of large loads and nearby generating facilities, and wants rules to allow the paired generator to sit within a defined number of electrical buses rather than requiring the same point of interconnection. This mirrors SPP's HILL framework, which allows up to two substations of separation for non-765 kV generators.
quotes: It is essential that any large load rulemaking facilitate the ability to serve new loads with grid-connected generation in a manner similar to the SPP HILL Proposal.
the load also may be located within a specified number of buses to ensure that system impacts will be limited to a local area.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: CPP's integrated three-year planning cycle merges the transmission planning and generator interconnection processes into a single workflow, satisfying the ANOPR's joint-study principle while going beyond its specific recommendations.
quotes: CPP 'eliminat[es] the silos between the transmission planning process and the generator interconnection process, synthesizing and streamlining them into one recurring three-year planning cycle.'

letters.desc: Terraflux agrees that co-located and near-located load-plus-generation facilities should be studied together as a single hybrid request rather than split into separate load and generation studies.
quotes: We agree with the third principle's assertion that both co-located and near-located load plus generation facilities should be studied together as hybrid facilities, rather than forced to be studied as one separate load interconnection request and one separate generation interconnection request. We propose that 'near-located' means within three busbar substations of each other, while 'co-located' means within the same busbar substation.

letters.desc: Interconnection studies should incorporate enforceable curtailment commitments and multi-day load-shifting capabilities so that flexible loads are not over-studied relative to their actual grid impact.
quotes: TBA strongly recommends that interconnection studies explicitly incorporate enforceable curtailment commitments and multi-day load-shifting capabilities.

letters.desc: Tract supports studying load and co-located generation together at the same point of interconnection. It insists this be at both parties' option and designed to produce faster or cheaper outcomes, not imposed as a requirement.
quotes: Tract supports DOE's proposal to study load and hybrid facilities together with generating facilities located at the same point of interconnection. Such joint study process should be at the option of both the load and generation customer and should be designed in such a way to result in faster and/or less costly interconnection for both the load and the generator.

letters.org: Utility Intervention Unit, New York State Department of Stat
letters.desc: The UIU supports studying large loads and hybrid facilities in the same process as generating facilities to ensure comparable, coordinated infrastructure planning.
quotes: UIU supports the ANOPR proposal to study load and hybrid facilities together with generating facilities.

letters.desc: Vantage supports joint study of hybrid facility load and generation components, noting that current independent sequential evaluations can produce inaccurate grid impact assessments and unnecessary network upgrade requirements.
quotes: Currently, many transmission and interconnection study processes involve independent evaluations at different times which can produce unintended results, including inaccurate assessments of impacts on the grid and resulting requirements for network upgrades that could have been avoided or mitigated by undertaking the studies in tandem.

letters.desc: The filers support the joint study of load and generation under Principle Three and ask that it explicitly extend to incremental distributed resources in the relevant grid area, regardless of whether those resources resemble utility-scale plants.
quotes: the existing ANOPR Principle Three, “load and hybrid facilities should be studied together with generating facilities,” should explicitly include study of incremental resources in the relevant grid area,16 whether or not those resources look like traditional utility-scale power plants.

letters.org: Wisconsin Electric Power CompanyWisconsin Public Service Corporation
letters.desc: WEC supports using the gross load amount as the default for studying large load interconnections, arguing it matches existing Commission precedent and accurately reflects actual transmission use even when co-located generation reduces net withdrawal.
quotes: the Commission should make the "gross" amount of load the default approach for studying large load interconnections consistent with existing Commission precedent.  This will ensure that co-located arrangements are appropriately studied based on their actual use of the transmission system, even if the load or generation has its withdrawal or injection rights based on the net capacity behind the meter.

letters.desc: Advanced Energy United supports studying new large loads together with co-located supply resources where they are electrically proximate, as this reduces network upgrades. It strongly opposes a loosely defined expedited pathway that would let generators bypass the standard queue, calling for strict eligibility criteria, limited interconnection service, and a sunset period similar to SPP's HILLGA framework.
quotes: However, a loosely defined load/supply resource interconnection pathway that provides an expedited pathway for generation interconnection without appropriate safeguards would result in undue discrimination and unjust and unreasonable rates.

This means (1) this expedited pathway should not confer the same interconnection service as is available to interconnection customers serving native load, and (2) this pathway should be available only to generation or storage resources that are not similarly situated to other interconnection customers in that they meet eligibility parameters that meaningfully, transparently, and objectively differentiate projects that proceed via expedited pathways from projects in the general queue.

To the extent that a new large load and new generation or storage resource are geographically and electrically proximate, studying them together would reduce network upgrades, lower costs, and reduce the need for critical supply chain components.

letters.desc: CAISO sees merit in a unified study process for loads and generators but cautions it could add complexity to processes recently overhauled by Order No. 2023. CAISO recommends preserving regional flexibility under the independent entity standard.
quotes: Providing a single study process for large load, hybrid, and generating facilities may simplify many aspects for transmission providers and developers.  At the same time, it could introduce new complexities to the interconnection study process and transmission planning process, both of which have been significantly reformed by recent Commission orders.

The longstanding approach of enabling transmission providers to propose tailored processes to meet regional needs under the independent entity standard will allow transmission providers to tailor their studies to ensure the orderly and timely interconnection of large loads.

letters.desc: Consumers Energy is concerned that changes to study processes for large loads and hybrid facilities could slow the interconnection of new generation, which the Administration has made a priority. The filer urges the Commission to evaluate those impacts carefully before directing any changes.
quotes: the Commission should carefully evaluate how such changes could impact and potentially slow the interconnection of new generation that the Administration has made a priority.

letters.desc: Duke Energy is open to coordinating load and generation evaluations in transmission planning but warns that integrating individual load studies with clustered generator interconnection studies introduces significant complexity. It questions whether the effort will speed or impede timely interconnection.
quotes: Duke Energy urges the Commission to consider whether the time needed to address the complexity and details of coordinated load and generation studies will help achieve faster interconnection of large loads or whether such an effort could actually impede timely interconnections of large loads at this pivotal moment.

letters.desc: LPPC supports studying load and generation together where practical but warns that mandatory joint study can disrupt existing processes and delay both generation and load interconnections in some regions.
quotes: While many utilities have found it useful to study new load and generation together, in some settings the introduction of large load into the study process will be disruptive of existing study processes and holds the potential to delay both generation and load interconnections.

letters.desc: The PA PUC objects to requiring load and hybrid facilities to be studied together with generating facilities as part of a broader set of reforms that collectively exceed FERC authority. However, it leaves open the possibility that limited paired-study guidance for true hybrid interconnections could be acceptable if it shortens timelines.
quotes: The recommendations that (1) load and hybrid facilities be studied together with generating facilities for efficient siting and be subject to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties; (2) hybrid facilities be studied based on the amount of injection and/or withdrawal rights requested to provide incentives for co-location with new generation facilities; (3) any hybrid interconnection install the system protection facilities necessary to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals that exceed the respective rights; (4) financial penalties for load facilities and hybrid facilities; (5) expedited consideration of interconnection studies of large loads and hybrid facilities that agree to be curtailable and dispatchable; and (6) that load and hybrid facilities should be responsible for 100% of the network upgrades that are assigned through the interconnection studies all have widespread economic and political ramifications.

Further guidance on paired interconnection studies could be welcome, subject to a more detailed proposed rule and opportunity for comment, if that guidance minimized the need for transmission buildout and interconnection study timelines due to the nature of that paired interconnection.

letters.desc: TAPS sees merit in studying large loads and generators in a single interconnection queue to limit gaming and undue discrimination, but notes that combining the queues requires working out cost allocation details across existing region-specific tariffs.
quotes: The use of a single interconnection queue to study Qualifying Large Loads and Hybrid Facilities together with generating facilities may facilitate identifying and avoiding undue discrimination or preference. Using separate study processes for different types of facilities could create opportunities for gaming the system or raise concerns about undue discrimination.

letters.desc: Alliant Energy opposes the ANOPR's netting proposal, arguing it oversimplifies operational realities because generation is intermittent while load must be served at all times. The filing recommends expedited study tracks like MISO's ERAS instead of netting as the correct way to integrate large loads quickly without understating system needs.
quotes: it is critical for the Commission to recognize that simply assuming generation and load offset each other is insufficient and could jeopardize reliability, affordability, and customer interests.

Netting assumes that load and generation at the same point of interconnection can offset one another for transmission planning purposes, but this oversimplification ignores critical operational realities.
Expedited interconnection processes like ERAS—not netting—are the right solution to integrate large loads efficiently and maintain a robust, reliable grid.

letters.desc: ATC urges separate studies for generation and load, and argues that imposing coordinated studies nationwide would undermine reliability and effectiveness. Local planning authorities should retain discretion over study sequencing.
quotes: ATC, along with other commenters, urges the Commission to separate studies for generation and load while preserving the flexibility for local planning authorities to rely upon their expertise to adjust sequencing and modeling.
Generation and load are functionally different and should be studied separately.
to the extent hybrid facilities are studied together, safeguards such as process matching and system protection facilities must be incorporated.

letters.desc: APS opposes the proposed 60-day study timeline as inadequate and calls for timelines determined in consultation with stakeholders and transmission planners.
quotes: the ANOPR's position of a 60-day study timeline might be inadequate dependent on the information required for the study itself, and the timeline should be determined in consultation with the stakeholders and transmission planners.

letters.desc: Requiring large load studies to be integrated with generation interconnection would disrupt CAISO's recently FERC-approved interconnection process enhancements, including the load-serving entity scoring mechanism that prioritizes generation and storage projects. This could delay procurement needed for state reliability and clean energy compliance.
quotes: adding this new layer of study processes would impact CAISO's recent interconnection process enhancements, approved by FERC last year, and their interaction with the CAISO Transmission Planning Process (TPP).

letters.desc: Entergy opposes any uniform federal interconnection queue for loads, arguing it would be inefficient and litigation-prone. Instead, utilities should be allowed to propose region-specific study processes through FPA Section 205 filings.
quotes: the Commission should allow individual utilities to submit proposals that specifically address the technical details involved in studying new loads or the requirement of operational limitations.

the Commission should eschew any formal or uniform federal queue requirement for loads.  A one-size-fits-all, Commission-regulated queue process has the potential to be inefficient, and fraught with litigation and conflict.

letters.desc: The filer resists studying loads together with generators on a mandatory basis, because generator study timelines cannot meet the tight schedules large loads face. Any inclusion in the joint cluster process should be optional or avoided entirely.
quotes: to the extent any final rule arising out of this proceeding contemplates including qualifying loads in the Order No. 2023-mandated cluster study process, such inclusion should be optional.
the strict and often lengthy study timelines for generator interconnection may not be practically feasible with the tight timelines for the interconnection of large loads
the Commission should consider not including loads in that process at all due to the time pressures described above.

letters.desc: In MISO, load and generation are studied separately because they have distinct reliability impacts. The MISO Transmission Owners say that more information is needed before they can support any joint-study mandate, and that any reform must preserve this separation for planning and metering purposes.
quotes: In order to comment meaningfully on the Third Principle, more information is needed.  In the MISO region, load integration and generation interconnection are studied separately because they have separate impacts on the bulk electric system.

letters.org: New York Transmission OwnersCentral Hudson Gas & Electric CorporationNew York Power Authority ,New York State Electric & Gas Corp. and Rochester Gas and El ,Niagara Mohawk d/b/a/ National Grid ,Consolidated Edison Company of New York, Inc. and Orange and ,Long Island Power Authority ,
letters.desc: The NYTOs oppose forcing large-load requests into fixed generator interconnection cluster study windows. In New York, missed application windows delay service by up to two years. They favor separate, parallel load cluster processes with cross-checks to the generator queue where needed, with each region maintaining discretion over study design.
quotes: Large-load requests should not be forced into generator cluster studies unless regional circumstances support doing so.

letters.org: North Carolina Utilities Commission Public Staff
letters.desc: Adding load into the generation study process risks restudies and delays when load projects drop out or seek material changes, undermining the value of the studies.
quotes: adding a new layer to the study process will inevitably cause restudies, delays, and inaccurate studies when projects inevitably either drop out of the queue or seek material changes to their load profiles.

letters.desc: ODEC opposes studying load and hybrid facilities together with generation because generators have outages and different retirement schedules, meaning the grid must still be designed to carry the full load independently. Separate studies produce more accurate planning and avoid masking infrastructure needs.
quotes: ODEC does not support studying load and hybrid facilities together with generation facilities.
Generators experience both planned and unplanned outages; thus, the transmission facilities must be evaluated with only the load operational, not the generation.

letters.desc: PG&E opposes mandating a single joint study approach for load, hybrids, and generation. It says overburdened generation queues in some regions would worsen if new load studies are folded in, and that utilities and RTOs should choose their own coordination methods.
quotes: PG&E recommends that the Commission not mandate a single study approach but instead allow individual utilities and/or Regional Transmission Organizations and Independent System Operators ('RTO/ISO') to decide the most efficient way to coordinate planning.

Adding into this mix load and hybrid facility interconnections may only exacerbate this problem. In some parts of the country, load and hybrid facility interconnection requests may be able to be seamlessly added to the generation interconnection process. In other parts of the country, adding this new requirement to an already overburdened process may be detrimental.

letters.org: PSEG CompaniesPSEG Energy Resources & Trade LLCPSEG Power LLC ,Public Service Electric and Gas Company ,
letters.desc: PSEG opposes folding resource adequacy analysis into individual co-location interconnection studies. It argues resource adequacy is a system-wide concern that RTOs should address at the regional level, not through project-specific RMR studies.
quotes: it would be inappropriate to consider resource adequacy issues in the study process for co-located load/hybrid arrangements.
